most_relevant.description:
I will say that I find navigation in this airport to be easy. The signage and staff works efficiently together. I always knew where to go and what to do—thank you CDG for that.

Moving on, I found this airport to be a mixed bag—nearly each attribute is both good and bad. The style and design of this airport is both modern and attractive, while other parts appear terribly outdated (red carpet, I’m talking to you!). While there are a large number of touristy cafes, many of the exact same items can be found at “grab ‘n go” retail shops at half the cost—use caution.

The worst part about this airport, imo, is the gate areas. Seating is not near enough and pathways are narrow. This means that if you need a seat at peak travel times, there will not be one available. This also means that those narrow pathways are completely clogged with waiting passengers—making navigation in the gate areas slow and difficult.

A good number of airports have impressed me in many ways.  CDG is not one of them. Review based on layovers only at international terminal 2F. I’ve yet to exit or enter CDG. My opinion could change if/when experiencing a different terminal.

This is one of the prettiest airports I’ve ever been to. The architecture is really impressive and feels modern and well designed.

The waiting and lounge areas are bright, spacious, and beautiful, which makes the whole travel experience much more pleasant. A great first (or last) impression of Paris.

The Paris airport is clean and very innovative. We flew United back to US. Check in process was smooth especially with Premier and No. 1 access. Security wasn’t too bad. Lots of high end shopping and stores for those that like that. The seating areas by the gates are super nice though and they even have gaming areas for kids. Sadly no United, Amex or Sapphire lounges in Terminal 1. Super cool airport overall.

Nice airport just had a connection there. I had to go thru security twice easy. Just be prepared to walk a little. When I bought food and souvenirs they had to scan my boarding pass. They had some arcades games to play, but no pinball. C'mon man need a pinball machine in there let's go terminal 2e.

Terminal 1 is one of the airport’s most distinctive terminals, known for its circular design. The terminal is modern, brighter, and organized. The central building design with satellite boarding gates is unique, and moving walkways connect different sections. Shopping and dining options include duty‑free stores, luxury boutiques, cafés, and casual restaurants. Seating areas are comfortable.

CDG is absolutely massive! I've traveled quite a bit to many airports and this one has to be the largest. It's quite beautiful for the most part with impressive architectural features, various well thought out amenities, and ships and restaurants all over the place.

The size of the facility can be problematic. The layout isn't particularly intuitive, and getting from one place to another can be cumbersome. If you have a layover, or you aren't familiar with where you'll be going, do yourself a favor and give yourself plenty of time to figure things out while you're there. A few years ago I had a layover here when returning to the US from Italy and my first flight was delayed. I only had 30 minutes to get to my next gate and my wife and I literally sprinted for the full 30 minutes! It was not a good time!!

This trip however, we had a 7hr layover so we had plenty of time to really experience the airport. The bag storage was very convenient, although it's a bit of a walk. If you want to take advantage you'll need to walk to the train station (there are two separate locations but both are next to the train station).

Overall, it's a great airport as long as you aren't in a rush.

Nice airport. The rental car drop off is right at the airport, no need for a taxi or bus shuttle. Just a quick walk and an elevator.  The airport signage is good and clear.  We'll organized, staff is English speaking which is very helpful.  The ques looked like they moved quickly. We were priority line which went even faster.

The train to the airport was packed, hot and slow. It decided to terminate at the stop prior to our terminal. So we waited for another train. The walk to the airport is a slow slog, the JetBlue kiosks are antiquated, the lines endless. When you think you’re finally through - you got your bags passed security - the real horror begins: passport control.
The line snakes around over 8 times; well over 100 people.
And there was only. One. Window. Open.
We are seniors so they let us cut most of the line; if not, I may have fainted from the heat and close quarters. Regardless of how old I am.
Once through, you really feel like you accomplished something…
DEFINITELY arrive 2 1/2 hours prior to take-off. I highly recommend it.

text_blocks.snippet: For general passenger inquiries and support at Paris Charles de Gaulle International Airport (CDG), you can utilize the following official contact resources provided by the airport operator, Aéroports de Paris (ADP).

list.snippet: Within France: Dial 3950. (Cost is €0.35/min including tax from a landline, available from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM local time. Operator surcharges may apply).
Official Website: Access flight details, real-time alerts, and standard services on the Paris Aéroport Official CDG Portal.
Online Contact & Complaint Form: If you need to log a formal information request, complaint, or feedback, you can fill out the official passenger Paris Aéroport Contact Form.

Lost & Found: If you lost a personal item inside the terminal buildings (excluding checked baggage), you must submit a mandatory Paris Aéroport Lost Property Report online before visiting the physical office. For lost checked luggage, you must contact your specific airline directly.

Mobility & PRM Assistance: Free assistance for passengers with reduced mobility or disabilities can be requested at least 48 hours before departure via your airline or through the Paris Aéroport Mobility Assistance Desk.
Emergency Medical Center: Accessible 24/7 at the airport by dialing +33 1 48 62 28 00 or +33 1 74 25 12 12.

text_blocks.snippet: Are you trying to resolve a specific issue like a lost item, planning mobility assistance, or trying to contact a specific airline operating out of CDG? Let me know so I can provide the direct link or form.

sanitizedResponse.reconstructed_markdown:
For general passenger inquiries and support at Paris Charles de Gaulle International Airport \(CDG\), you can utilize the following official contact resources provided by the airport operator, [Aéroports de Paris \(ADP\)](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en).

### 📞 Telephone & Helplines

- Within France: Dial 3950. \(Cost is €0.35/min including tax from a landline, available from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM local time. Operator surcharges may apply\).
- International Calls: Dial \+33 1 70 36 39 50. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/\)

### 🌐 Digital & Written Communication

- Official Website: Access flight details, real\-time alerts, and standard services on the [Paris Aéroport Official CDG Portal](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/cdg).
- Online Contact & Complaint Form: If you need to log a formal information request, complaint, or feedback, you can fill out the official passenger [Paris Aéroport Contact Form](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/group/strategy/hub-one/contact).
- Mailing Address: \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/cdg\)

### 🧳 Specific Passenger Services

- Lost & Found: If you lost a personal item inside the terminal buildings \(excluding checked baggage\), you must submit a mandatory [Paris Aéroport Lost Property Report](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at-the-airport/services/luggage-lost-property/cdg) online before visiting the physical office. For lost checked luggage, you must contact your specific airline directly. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at\-the\-airport/services/luggage\-lost\-property/cdg\)
- Mobility & PRM Assistance: Free assistance for passengers with reduced mobility or disabilities can be requested at least 48 hours before departure via your airline or through the [Paris Aéroport Mobility Assistance Desk](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/flight-preparation/prm-assistance/prm-accessibility).
- Emergency Medical Center: Accessible 24/7 at the airport by dialing \+33 1 48 62 28 00 or \+33 1 74 25 12 12. \(https://parisjetaime.com/\)

Are you trying to resolve a specific issue like a lost item, planning mobility assistance, or trying to contact a specific airline operating out of CDG? Let me know so I can provide the direct link or form.

The official terminal and service maps for Charles de Gaulle International Airport \(CDG\) are hosted directly by the airport's official operating authority, [Paris Aéroport](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at-the-airport/terminals-map/cdg). Because CDG is one of Europe's largest and most complex airport hubs, maps are divided by specific terminal buildings and functional needs to help you navigate efficiently. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at\-the\-airport/terminals\-map/cdg\)

### 🗺️ Interactive & Master Airport Maps

- Interactive Services Map: To look up specific boarding gates, lounges, shops, restaurants, or baggage claim areas floor\-by\-floor, use the dynamic [Paris Aéroport Interactive CDG Map](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at-the-airport/services/services-map/cdg).
- General Layout Overview: Review general transit connections, terminal locations, and the CDGVAL automated metro shuttle paths on the Paris Aéroport CDG Terminal Guide Overview. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/\)

### 🛫 Terminal\-Specific Maps

You can download or view static layouts for each individual terminal group via the Paris Aéroport Terminal Directory: \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at\-the\-airport/terminals\-map/cdg\)

- Terminal 1: Designed around a circular central building with seven stories connected to five boarding satellites. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at\-the\-airport/terminals\-map/cdg\)
- Terminal 2 \(ABCD\): Covers halls 2A, 2B, 2C, and 2D, which allow free pedestrian movement through the public side. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at\-the\-airport/terminals\-map/cdg\)
- Terminal 2 \(EFG\): Covers halls 2E \(including its large international departure concourses\), 2F, and the separate 2G building. \(Note: Terminal 2G is reachable via the free N2 shuttle bus from Terminal 2F\). \(https://www.parisinsidersguide.com/\)
- Terminal 3: Separated into two individual buildings for dedicated departure and arrival operations. \(https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/at\-the\-airport/terminals\-map/cdg\)

### 🚗 Parking & Ground Transportation Maps

- Driving & Parking: If you are arriving by car or rental, track your route to the closest terminal lot using the [Paris Aéroport Official Car Park Map](https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/transport-parking/by-car/parking/map/cdg).
- Airline Lounges: If flying with US\-based or alliance partner airlines, you can cross\-reference terminal amenities with the [Delta Air Lines CDG Lounge Finder](https://www.delta.com/us/en/airports/europe/paris-sky-club-airport-map) to view locations for Air France lounges spread across Terminals 2B, 2C, 2D, 2E, 2F, and 2G. \(https://www.delta.com/us/en/airports/europe/paris\-sky\-club\-airport\-map\)

To help you find the right map layout, could you share:

- Which airline you are flying with?
- Whether you are arriving, departing, or transferring during a layover?
